back: Recruiting, moving or holding people by force, threats or deception in order to exploit them.
Helping a willing person to cross a border illegally, usually for payment.
Forcing a person to work in a household with no freedom and little or no pay.
Moving legally with full information, valid documents, a real contract and contacts at home.

front: What is the main international agreement against trafficking?
back: The UN Trafficking in Persons (Palermo) Protocol, 2000.

front: When is the World Day against Trafficking in Persons?
Name four warning signs of a false job offer.
back: No contract, a fee to an agent, pressure to leave quickly, secrecy, the agent keeps your passport, pay too good to be true.

front: Give three differences between trafficking and smuggling.
back: Consent (none vs agreed); border (not needed vs always); after the journey (exploitation continues vs relationship ends).

front: Why is a trafficked person a victim even if they agreed to travel?
back: They agreed to a job, not to exploitation; they were deceived, controlled or forced.
